actions.description: Share what you have verified — who is on the road, which clip is fake, which rumour is moving — with every other team. Free, always available, and the cheapest thing that stops two teams answering the same crowd with different stories.

One lane opened through the blockade for food, fuel and medical convoys at set hours, agreed with the people holding the road and marked by VDOT. Keeps supplies moving without clearing anyone; only holds while the protesters agree to it.

available_to: Virginia National Guard, Southwest Task Force
actions.description: Deputies, with Guard support if it is requested, remove the blockade and reopen US-23. Fast and certain for the road; arrests on camera and a crowd that leaves angrier and comes back somewhere else.

actions.action_name: Signed Detour and Road Closure Plan
actions.description: Close the blocked segment, sign detours through Norton and Coeburn, and publish them. Moves traffic around the protest rather than through it; adds an hour to every supply run into the coalfields.

The Liaison asks the Governor to send the Guard to the coalfields. Free to request and the only way troops come; what they are sent to do has to be decided, and a request made public is its own message.

available_to: Virginia National Guard, Southwest Task Force
actions.description: Guard members posted at food and fuel distribution sites, unarmed or armed as the order says, so the sites can open. Protects the queue; turns every photo of the queue into a photo of soldiers.

available_to: Virginia National Guard, Southwest Task Force
actions.description: Guard vehicles escort supply convoys on the detour or through the negotiated lane. Gets trucks through; read by the protesters as the state arriving with force.

A signed agreement on who decides distribution in Wise County: the county's rules where they are published and fair, the state's where they are not, and a joint table for disputes. Ends the public fight over authority, if both sides sign.
Wise County adopts its own emergency distribution rules — who gets served first, how much, and at which sites. Local authority exercised in the open; defiance of the state if nobody agreed to it.

actions.action_name: Public Town Hall with Ground Rules
actions.description: A moderated county forum with published ground rules, a speakers' list and security outside the room. The grievance gets a hearing; a forum without rules is where the next fight starts.

One regional update on a fixed schedule — state, county, EMA and the utilities saying the same thing at the same hour. The single fastest cure for contradictory statements; only works if everyone uses it.
Publish, by county, what food, fuel and money went where last week and why. The direct answer to 'the state saved Roanoke and not us' — if the numbers do not say that.

actions.requires_approval: Governor's SW Virginia Liaison or SW Virginia EMA
actions.description: An alert over radio, TV and phones to everyone in the region. Reaches people the feeds do not; a broadcast that turns out wrong is the next rumour.
A newsroom desk that checks clips and claims within the hour and publishes what is known, what is not, and how it was checked. Beats a rumour only if it is faster than the rumour.
Forensic check of the clip and a documented request to the platforms to label or remove it. A finding a county official can cite; the platforms decide what they do with the request.
An hour of airtime with coalition speakers, officials and clergy on the same stage, moderated. The protest gets its case heard somewhere other than the road; a bad hour on air is worse than none.
The coalition names its demands in writing and the people authorised to negotiate them. Gives officials someone to talk to; a movement that speaks with one voice can also be held to what it said.
Coalition leaders and pastors ask the armed 'protection' groups to leave the sites and the road. The one ask only the community can make; if it fails, it fails in public.
Trained observers in visible vests at the blockade and the distribution sites, recording enforcement. Lowers the temperature on both sides; a documented abuse becomes evidence.

Published know-your-rights guidance, and a motion in court if enforcement or a county ordinance crosses the line. Protects the right to protest and to equal service; a court fight in the middle of an emergency is slow and loud.
Trained mediators bring the coalition, the county and the state to one table with an agreed agenda. The route to a lane or an end to the blockade that nobody is forced into.
Take every complaint about who was served and who was not, and publish what happened to each. Turns anger into cases that can be answered; a tracker nobody updates is proof of the grievance.
Pastors, fire chiefs and store owners carry the same verified update door to door in the hollows. Reaches people who believe no feed; slow and only as good as the update they carry.
Paired rural visits, a deputy on call for threatened staff, and a hotline for any clinician who is followed or confronted. Keeps the clinics open; nurses go out slower and fewer.
Crisis counsellors in the clinics, the churches and the distribution sites, and a line that answers. Meets the fear before it turns into the next confrontation; takes staff the clinics barely have.
Staff from Roanoke cover the coalfield clinics that are short. Keeps doors open; arrives as proof, to some, that the city is sending help only now.

Check the distribution sites' records against who was turned away and why, and publish what the audit finds. Answers the favouritism claim with evidence either way; an audit that finds favouritism has to be acted on.
